hook: A vending machine turns up in a Yokohama back alley with an 'out of order' sign taped to it. The premise is light, and most of the file is a test log you can read like a menu. Go in expecting a comedy and let the list decide when it stops being one.
whyItMatters: It is a clean example of the log format: the description sets one rule, and a long list of results does the storytelling. One entry has the machine dispense another numbered anomaly, a small moment where a self-contained object suddenly touches the wider archive. Objects like this are a big part of the cabinet-of-curiosities pleasure of browsing the Foundation.
thingsToNotice:
The log is arranged as an escalation: real products first, then plausible flavors no company makes, then food with strange chemistry, then packaging in no known language. The procedures are part of the joke, with yen purchase limits, a health review and compensation for confiscated snacks reading like an office policy.

Watch how the tone stays chirpy while the entries get stranger, and how the last item ends testing with almost no comment. That flat delivery hits harder than a warning would.

related.note: It comes out of this machine in the test log; read it to see what was in the can.
Another drink-dispensing machine with unpredictable results.
